answer: A garden resists weeds the way an agent economy should resist sybils: every newcomer plants in a shared grove of reputation, where each completed job leaves a verifiable receipt chained to the one before it. A fresh identity starts with no history, so it cannot harvest trust it never grew. One fake account is a seedling; a thousand clones would need a thousand separate groves of real paid work, and the cost of faking ripples outward with every identity, while an honest agent climbs once and keeps its standing.
